ei.title: Breaking the Cycle: Solutions to E-waste
ei.subject: 영어2

fullPassage: On her way to a study group meeting, Liz accidentally dropped her laptop on the street, seriously damaging it. Although it still turns on, the screen is cracked, and some keys are not working. She can have it repaired, but she is hesitating to do so. Sometimes repairs are expensive, and they often take a long time. Besides, the laptop is about five years old. In this case, getting rid of the old one and purchasing a new one might seem like a more reasonable option. In reality, however, it may not be the best thing to do. If Liz throws her laptop in the trash, she will be contributing to a serious problem: e-waste. What exactly is e-waste? The term refers to discarded electronic devices and electrical appliances. Due to toxic materials contained in these products, such as lead, e-waste is a serious health and environmental hazard. To make matters worse, the amount of e-waste produced each year is increasing at an alarming rate. In 2021, a total of 57.4 million metric tons* of e-waste was generated worldwide, which was a 37% increase from 2014, the year when data about e-waste was first collected. Experts predict that by 2030, the amount of e-waste generated annually will have doubled in just 16 years. For this reason, efforts are being made to address this problem, most of which are focused on making products easier to repair. Let’s take a look at some practical approaches from around the world. Right-to-Repair Movement: Empowering Consumers One reason many people dispose of their damaged devices is that they are too difficult to repair. For example, a device may be difficult to disassemble, or its manufacturer may require that it be brought to an official service center to be fixed. Many companies do not allow their customers to take their damaged items to third-party repair shops. What is more, some products are intentionally designed to be difficult to repair. It is common for consumers to be unable to acquire the instructions for how to fix their items or the parts needed to complete repairs. The right-to-repair movement is trying to solve these problems by promoting legislation that states the following: If you own a product, you have the right to fix it yourself or bring it to a technician of your choice. To protect the rights of consumers, the right-to-repair movement demands four things. First, companies must make information about their products available to everyone. Second, third parties, including individuals, should be able to obtain the parts and tools required to make repairs. Third, the practice of preventing consumers from installing custom software on their own devices should be prohibited by law. Finally, it demands that manufacturers design devices in a way that makes repairs as easy as possible. Advocates of the movement say that if all these goals are accomplished, far less e-waste will be generated. Thanks to their efforts, more than 40 states in the U.S. have begun working on right-to-repair legislation. This movement is gaining a growing influence in Europe as well, with more and more countries joining the cause. Repairability Index: Information at a Glance In January 2021, the French government passed a bill that requires that every manufacturer include a “repairability index” on five categories of electronic devices and electrical appliances: smartphones, laptops, washing machines, televisions, and lawn mowers. Using a score ranging from 0 to 10, as well as a color-coded system, the index lets consumers see how easily the product can be repaired before they purchase it. The index takes into account several elements, including the availability of repair information, the ease of disassembly, and the price of spare parts. A low number on a bright red label means that repairing the product will be difficult, whereas a high number on a green label indicates that the product is easy to repair. The index was designed to have two positive effects. Firstly, it allows consumers to make informed decisions when purchasing new devices and appliances. Secondly, it encourages manufacturers to make their products easier to repair. As a result, with fewer electronic and electrical items ending up in its landfills, France can expect to make a transition to a more sustainable society in the near future. The impact of the index, however, is likely to spread far beyond France. We live in a global economy, and any company that wants to sell its appliances on the French market will need to label its products according to the repairability index. If the index is successful, we can anticipate seeing more countries around the world following France’s innovative lead. Repair Cafés: It Takes a Community When consumers are given the right tools and materials, along with some helpful advice, they can repair much of the damage that occurs to electronic products by themselves. That is why Repair Cafés were started. They are free meeting places where people can gather together and fix their broken devices. The cafés are staffed by volunteer experts who can give technical advice and teach people how to fix things. The first Repair Café was opened in the Netherlands in the city of Amsterdam in 2009. It was such a success that the idea soon spread to neighboring countries. Before long, there were Repair Cafés in over 30 countries around the world. Along with preventing damaged items from becoming e-waste, these cafés also encourage people to share their invaluable skills and knowledge about the repair and maintenance of electronics. They continue to grow in popularity, with more and more people signing up to volunteer. By providing spaces where people can learn, Repair Cafés enable individuals to maintain their devices and extend their life spans. Furthermore, they foster a sustainable perspective that can have a huge positive impact on our future. Do you remember Liz, the girl who dropped her laptop? Imagine she lived in a world where repairing damaged devices and appliances was simply part of everyday life. If that were the case, her options wouldn’t be limited to paying for expensive repairs or throwing away her laptop and buying a new one. She would be able to order the necessary parts online and replace them herself. Alternatively, she could bring her damaged device to the nearest Repair Café to get advice on how to fix it. Repairing it probably wouldn’t be very hard, and she likely would have purchased a laptop with a high repairability score. In fact, this sustainable world is a future we can all enjoy if we work toward it together. Even more importantly, it is a future in which people will generate far less e-waste, making our planet a cleaner, healthier place for everyone.

det.korean: ② includes → include: 요구를 나타내는 require의 that절은 '(should) + 동사원형'이므로 include

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ wasteful(낭비적인) → sustainable(지속 가능한): 폐기물이 줄어 더 지속 가능한 사회로 간다
det.analysis:

✅ ③ landfills(매립지): 전자·전기 제품이 '매립지'로 가는 양이 줄어든다는 문맥에 적절
❌ ④ wasteful(낭비적인) → sustainable(지속 가능한): 매립되는 제품이 줄어든 결과이므로 '더 지속 가능한(sustainable) 사회'로의 전환이 와야 한다. '낭비적인(wasteful) 사회'는 정반대라 문맥에 어긋난다 ← 정답
det.tip: sustainable(지속 가능한) ↔ wasteful(낭비적인). fewer items → sustainable society

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ accidentally(우연히) → intentionally(의도적으로): 일부 제품은 수리하기 어렵게 '의도적으로' 설계된다
det.analysis:
✅ ① dispose: 'many people dispose of their damaged devices'에서 손상된 기기를 '버린다(dispose of)'는 문맥에 적절
✅ ② official: 'brought to an official service center'에서 '공식' 서비스 센터로 가져가야 한다는 문맥에 적절
❌ ③ accidentally(우연히) → intentionally(의도적으로): 바로 앞에서 기업들이 수리를 어렵게 만든다고 했고, 'some products are ___ designed to be difficult to repair'는 제조사가 일부러 그렇게 만든다는 뜻이다. 따라서 '우연히'가 아니라 '의도적으로(intentionally)'가 맞다 ← 정답
✅ ④ acquire: 'unable to acquire the instructions ~ or the parts'에서 설명서나 부품을 '구하다(acquire)'라는 문맥에 적절
det.tip: intentionally(의도적으로) ↔ accidentally(우연히). designed to be difficult = 의도적

det.korean: 빈칸에 far less e-waste(훨씬 더 적은 전자폐기물)가 적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① much more e-waste(훨씬 더 많은 전자폐기물): 네 가지 요구가 수리를 쉽게 만드는 것이므로 폐기물이 '늘어난다'는 것은 정반대
✅ ② far less e-waste(훨씬 더 적은 전자폐기물): 정보 공개·부품 제공·수리하기 쉬운 설계 등 모든 목표(all these goals)가 이뤄지면 제품을 오래 쓰게 되어 폐기물이 '훨씬 줄어든다'가 자연스럽다 ← 정답
❌ ③ a serious hazard(심각한 위험): '위험이 발생할 것이다'는 흐름과 어긋남
❌ ④ a higher price(더 높은 가격): 가격 이야기는 이 문맥에 없음
det.tip: goals accomplished(수리가 쉬워짐) → far less e-waste will be generated

questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.analysis:
① 본문 'In January 2021, the French government passed a bill that requires ~ a repairability index'와 일치
② 본문 'Using a score ranging from 0 to 10, as well as a color-coded system'과 일치
③ 본문 'the availability of repair information, the ease of disassembly, and the price of spare parts'와 일치
④ 본문 'A low number on a bright red label means that repairing the product will be difficult'에서 낮은 점수의 빨간 라벨은 수리가 '어렵다'는 뜻이다. '쉽다'는 불일치 ← 정답
det.tip: 낮은 점수·빨간색 = 수리 어려움(difficult), 높은 점수·녹색 = 수리 쉬움

ch: 프랑스 정부는 2021년 1월에 수리 가능성 지수에 관한 법안을 통과시켰다.
이 지수는 0에서 10까지의 점수와 색상 표시 체계를 사용한다.
지수는 수리 정보의 입수 가능성, 분해의 용이성, 예비 부품 가격 등을 고려한다.
낮은 점수의 빨간색 라벨은 제품을 수리하기 쉽다는 것을 의미한다.

questions.passage: The cafés are staffed by volunteer experts who can give technical advice and teach people how to fix things.  The first Repair Café was opened in the Netherlands in the city of Amsterdam in 2009.  It was such a success that the idea soon spread to neighboring countries.  Before long, there were Repair Cafés in over 30 countries around the world.  Along with preventing damaged items from becoming e-waste, these cafés also encourage people to share their invaluable skills and knowledge about the repair and maintenance of electronics.  They continue to grow in popularity, with more and more people signing up to volunteer.  By providing spaces where people can learn, Repair Cafés enable individuals to maintain their devices and extend their life spans.  Furthermore, they foster a sustainable perspective that can have a huge positive impact on our future.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.analysis:
① 본문 'The first Repair Café was opened in the Netherlands in the city of Amsterdam'에서 최초의 Café는 '네덜란드' 암스테르담에서 열렸다. '독일'은 불일치
② 본문 'there were Repair Cafés in over 30 countries around the world'와 일치 ← 정답
③ 본문 'They continue to grow in popularity, with more and more people signing up to volunteer'에서 인기가 계속 커지고 자원봉사자도 늘고 있다. '시들해진다'는 불일치
④ 본문 'these cafés also encourage people to share their invaluable skills and knowledge'에서 기술 공유를 '장려'한다. '금지한다'는 불일치
det.tip: 네덜란드에서 시작 → 30개국 이상 확산, 기술 공유 장려, 인기 상승

ch: 최초의 Repair Café는 2009년 독일에서 문을 열었다.
Repair Café는 전 세계 30개국 이상으로 퍼져 나갔다.
Repair Café의 인기는 자원봉사자 감소로 점차 시들해지고 있다.
Repair Café는 수리 기술의 공유를 금지하고 전문가만 수리하게 한다.

questions.passage: The right-to-repair movement, which ①<u>has gained</u> influence worldwide, demands several important changes. First, companies must make information about their products available to everyone and ②<u>allow</u> third parties to obtain the necessary parts. Repair Cafés, ③<u>where</u> volunteers help people fix broken devices, have also spread to many countries. These efforts, all of which ④<u>aims</u> to reduce e-waste, are becoming more popular every year.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ aims → aim: all of which의 which가 가리키는 것은 efforts(복수)이므로 복수 동사 aim
det.analysis:
✅ ① has gained: 'The right-to-repair movement, which has gained influence worldwide'에서 선행사 movement(단수)에 맞는 현재완료(has p.p.)로 적절
✅ ② allow: 'companies must make information ~ and allow third parties'에서 조동사 must에 걸리는 동사원형(make ~ and allow) 병렬로 적절
✅ ③ where: 'Repair Cafés, where volunteers help people fix broken devices'에서 장소(Cafés)를 받고 뒤 절이 완전하므로 관계부사 where로 적절
❌ ④ aims → aim: 'These efforts, all of which ___ to reduce e-waste'에서 all of which의 which는 앞의 efforts(복수)를 가리킨다. 따라서 단수 aims가 아니라 복수 aim이 맞다. all을 단수로 착각하지 말 것 ← 정답
det.tip: all of which의 수는 which가 가리키는 선행사(efforts, 복수)에 맞춘다 → aim

questions.passage: What exactly is e-waste?  The term refers to discarded electronic devices and electrical appliances.  Due to toxic materials contained in these products, such as lead, e-waste is a serious health and environmental hazard.  To make matters worse, the amount of e-waste produced each year is increasing at an alarming rate.
questions.stem: 위 글에 따르면, 전자폐기물이 매년 늘어나는 속도가 걱정스러울 만큼 빠르다는 것을 나타내는 형용사를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (1단어, 영어로)

det.analysis: 본문 'the amount of e-waste produced each year is increasing at an alarming rate'에서 전자폐기물의 양이 '걱정스러운(alarming)' 속도로 늘고 있다고 했다. 빠른 증가에 대한 우려를 나타내는 형용사는 alarming이다.
det.tip: at an alarming rate(걱정스러울 만큼 빠른 속도로)에서 alarming을 찾습니다.

questions.passage: The cafés are staffed by volunteer experts who can give technical advice and teach people how to fix things.  The first Repair Café was opened in the Netherlands in the city of Amsterdam in 2009.  It was such a success that the idea soon spread to neighboring countries.  Before long, there were Repair Cafés in over 30 countries around the world.
questions.stem: 위 글에 따르면, Repair Café에서 사람들에게 기술적인 조언을 해 주고 수리 방법을 가르쳐 주는 이들을 가리키는 표현을 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (2단어, 영어로)

det.analysis: 본문 'The cafés are staffed by volunteer experts who can give technical advice and teach people how to fix things.'에서 기술적 조언을 해 주고 수리 방법을 가르치는 이들은 '자원봉사 전문가들(volunteer experts)'이다.
det.tip: staffed by volunteer experts who can give technical advice에서 volunteer experts를 찾습니다.

questions.passage: By __________ (provide) spaces where people can learn, Repair Cafés enable individuals to maintain their devices and extend their life spans. Furthermore, they foster a sustainable perspective that can have a huge positive impact on our future.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 흐름에 맞도록 괄호 안에 주어진 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (1단어, 영어로)

det.analysis: 구문 분석: 'By ___ (provide) spaces where people can learn'에서 빈칸은 전치사 By의 목적어 자리다. 전치사 뒤에는 동명사가 와야 하므로 동사원형 provide를 providing으로 바꿔야 한다. 'By + 동명사'는 '~함으로써'라는 수단을 나타낸다.
det.tip: 전치사(By) + 동명사(-ing): By providing spaces(공간을 제공함으로써)

questions.passage: For this reason, efforts are being made to address this problem, most of which are focused on making products easier to repair.  Let’s take a look at some practical approaches from around the world.  Right-to-Repair Movement: Empowering Consumers One reason many people dispose of their damaged devices is that they are too difficult to repair.  For example, a device may be difficult to disassemble, or its manufacturer may require that it be brought to an official service center to be fixed.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① 전자폐기물(e-waste)의 심각성을 제시하고, 그 해결책들이 '제품을 수리하기 쉽게 만드는 데(making products easier to repair)' 초점을 둔다고 밝힌 뒤 세계 각국의 접근법을 소개하므로 글 전체의 주제로 적절 ← 정답
❌ ② 수리 비용 절약은 Liz의 사례 도입부일 뿐 전체 주제가 아님
❌ ③ 무역 정책은 본문에 없는 내용
❌ ④ 구매 시 디자인 요소는 글의 핵심이 아님
det.tip: e-waste 문제 + 'efforts ~ focused on making products easier to repair'가 주제의 핵심입니다.

ch: 전자폐기물 문제를 줄이기 위해 제품 수리를 쉽게 만들려는 다양한 노력
노트북이 고장 났을 때 수리 비용을 절약하는 개인적인 방법
프랑스가 전자제품 수출을 늘리기 위해 도입한 무역 정책
새 전자기기를 구매할 때 고려해야 할 디자인 요소들

questions.passage: She would be able to order the necessary parts online and replace them herself.  Alternatively, she could bring her damaged device to the nearest Repair Café to get advice on how to fix it.  Repairing it probably wouldn’t be very hard, and she likely would have purchased a laptop with a high repairability score.  In fact, this sustainable world is a future we can all enjoy if we work toward it together.  Even more importantly, it is a future in which people will generate far less e-waste, making our planet a cleaner, healthier place for everyone.
questions.stem: 위 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① 글은 교체보다 수리를 권하므로 요지와 반대
❌ ② 본문은 소비자·시민의 참여도 강조하므로 '전적으로 정부·대기업 책임'은 과도
✅ ③ 본문 'this sustainable world is a future we can all enjoy if we work toward it together ~ people will generate far less e-waste'에서 수리가 일상이 되면 전자폐기물이 크게 줄어 더 지속 가능한 미래를 만들 수 있다는 것이 요지 ← 정답
❌ ④ 5년 경과 시 교체는 Liz 사례의 세부일 뿐 요지가 아님
det.tip: repairing ~ part of everyday life → far less e-waste → sustainable future가 요지입니다.

ch: 손상된 기기는 수리하기보다 새 제품으로 교체하는 것이 더 합리적이다.
전자폐기물 문제의 해결은 전적으로 정부와 대기업의 책임이다.
수리를 일상화하면 전자폐기물을 크게 줄여 더 지속 가능한 미래를 만들 수 있다.
노트북은 5년이 지나면 반드시 새것으로 교체해야 한다.

questions.passage: Firstly, it allows consumers to make informed decisions when purchasing new devices and appliances.  Secondly, __________.  As a result, with fewer electronic and electrical items ending up in its landfills, France can expect to make a transition to a more sustainable society in the near future.  The impact of the index, however, is likely to spread far beyond France.  We live in a global economy, and any company that wants to sell its appliances on the French market will need to label its products according to the repairability index.  If the index is successful, we can anticipate seeing more countries around the world following France’s innovative lead.
questions.stem:
위 글의 내용을 바탕으로, 다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 조건에 따라 영작하시오. (영어로)

'그것은 제조업체가 자신의 제품을 더 수리하기 쉽게 만들도록 장려한다.'

[조건]
(1) easier, encourages, it, make, manufacturers, products, repair, their, to, to를 모두 사용할 것
(2) 정확히 10단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: it encourages manufacturers to make their products easier to repair
det.analysis:
구문 분석:
- it(주어) + encourages(동사): 그것은 장려한다
- encourage + 목적어 + to부정사: 'encourages manufacturers to make ~'(제조업체가 ~하도록 장려하다)
- make + 목적어 + 형용사: 'make their products easier'(제품을 더 쉽게 만들다)
- to repair(수리하기)가 easier를 뒤에서 한정
- 순서대로 놓으면 it / encourages / manufacturers / to / make / their / products / easier / to / repair
det.tip: encourage + O + to부정사 / make + O + 형용사. easier to repair(수리하기 더 쉬운)

questions.wa: it encourages manufacturers to make their products easier to repair
accept: it encourages manufacturers to make their products easier to repair
